rationale: mandel-2 is a tiny, compute-bound Mandelbrot benchmark dominated by a single hot floating-point iteration loop with few functions and no meaningful call graph or data structures. Cheap, correct arithmetic-transforming passes are prioritized: SUB gets the highest security/diversity weights because instruction substitution obscures the FP/kernel arithmetic at negligible runtime and size cost, and SPLIT is favored as a low-risk basic-block diversifier that composes well with SUB. Cost-sensitive passes are deliberately down-weighted on their benefit dimensions and up-weighted on their cost dimensions: BCF and FLA would sit directly in the per-pixel inner loop, so their high RuntimeCost weights (0.9/0.85) suppress application where overhead would be severe, and FLA additionally carries an elevated CorrectnessRisk weight since flattening FP-loop control flow risks altering iteration behavior. IBR and IGV are kept at moderate weight — indirect branching and global-variable indirection add useful static-analysis resistance on the control-flow-dense loop body without dominating runtime, but are not critical for a single-function workload. ICALL is effectively disabled (low benefit, high runtime and correctness weights) because the program has almost no call sites to indirect, so it would only add dispatch overhead and miscompilation risk in the hot loop.
